Two schedules that merge (for example a 3-day and a 2-day) show as one day-by-day list with a merge row. The second schedule plays its own rounds 1 to merge round minus 1, then the primary's from the merge round on. A player's choice is stored on `registrations.schedule_id`, which stays the primary until WS06; a test shows a new entry still gets it from the trigger.

- **Where the member discount lived (step 15).** Re-ran the grep before the change; slices 10 to 14 had moved some hits. `functions/utils/pricing.ts` and `src/lib/pricing.ts` are one-line re-exports and needed no edit. `registrations/[id].ts` and the POST in `admin/tournaments.ts` had no hits (the create body schema is loose, so `memberDiscount` was already dropped there). `src/lib/api.ts` had one hit (line 603). The detail page's "LCA members save" note was at lines 1083 to 1091. `TournamentManagePage.tsx` and `FamilyRegistrationPanel.tsx` had the input and the per-player membership pricing. `HomePage.tsx` line 300 was a hit the plan missed ("discounted tournament entry"); fixed. `MembershipPage.tsx` has no discount wording, and no email template mentions a discount. After the change `member_discount`, `memberDiscount` and `isLcaMember` appear only in comments, the schema, `functions/types.ts` and the contract's tournament row and edit request; `no-member-price-surface.test.ts` pins that.

The field rule therefore names the director case, and tests cover an assigned director, a plain member assigned as director, another club's rep (assigned and not), a rep assigned to an LCA-run event, a plain member and a signed-out caller.

- **What the mover has to handle on the site (step 17).** Confirmed: the script searches every `.ts` and `.tsx` file under `src` and `test` (`SCAN_DIRS` and `CODE_EXTENSIONS` in `scripts/move-files.ts`), which covers `src/App.tsx`, `src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx` and `src/lib/viewOnly.tsx` as well as pages and components. The Vitest include `src/lib/scanner/**/*.test.ts` is unchanged, and no ESLint rule names `src/lib`.

It now scans the barrel, `http.ts` and every area `api.ts`, and compares the union with the paths from before the split. `test/unit/client-sections-audit.test.ts` read `src/lib/api.ts` by path too (see Deviations). `domain-boundaries.test.ts` uses the path only as an argument to its own helper, and the other mentions are comments.

So do `src/pages/ScholasticPage.tsx`, `src/pages/TournamentsPage.tsx`, `src/components/FacebookFeed.tsx` and `src/components/uscf/UscfSearchInput.tsx`. Route-audit has never covered them, and this step leaves them where they are; HomePage's call is WS03's.

- **What `src/lib/api.ts` held (step 18).** Confirmed before the split: three imports (`supabase`, the `RawScan` type, five contract types with `import type`), 182 exports and three private functions; no `export const`, default export, re-export or dynamic import. `supabase` was used only by `authHeaders`, `RawScan` only by `scanScoresheet`, and `exportQuery` only by the two member export calls. No statement had a comment after it on the same line, and none followed the last declaration.

In the installed version (0.5.3) it sets `react-refresh/only-export-components` to an error, with `allowConstantExport`. Three moved files already broke it before the move (`LCAMap.tsx` 8, `GradeConfirm.tsx` 3, `UsChessMembership.tsx` 1) and keep the same errors; `MembersTable.tsx`, `TournamentWizard.tsx` and `UscfSearchInput.tsx` export a type beside their component, which the rule allows. Every other moved file exports components only, and no file mixes exports that did not before. The area `index.ts` files are re-exports only and did not change.

Two tests pinned a moved path in a string (`client-sections-audit.test.ts` and `no-member-price-copy.test.ts`) and were fixed by hand.

The brief's WS04 section lists `TournamentsPage.tsx` ("split into view components"), WS05 `TournamentDetailPage.tsx`, WS08 `TournamentManagePage.tsx` and WS15 `ScannerPage.tsx`.

- **Can `wrangler pages dev` serve a built folder with the functions and the local database here (step 20).** Yes, with wrangler 4.112.0. A build folder other than `pages_build_output_dir` is accepted, and two servers share one `--persist-to` when each has its own `--inspector-port`. Wrangler prints "Proxy environment variables detected", and the server's own outbound fetches go through the proxy. Both servers shut down cleanly after the run.
- **Do bindings override `wrangler.toml` `[vars]` and `.dev.vars` (step 20).** `-b NAME=value` does; the startup list showed `SUPABASE_URL ("(hidden)")`. `--env-file` does not: wrangler 4.112 `pages dev` ignores it and still reads `.dev.vars`. So the config turns each line of `.dev.vars.a11y` into a `-b` flag and binds the five service keys empty, and a planted `.dev.vars` with sentinel values did not reach the servers.
- **Does `vite build --mode a11y` read `.env.a11y` (step 20).** It would, but a value in the process environment wins over the file, empty strings included (`loadEnv` in `node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js`, line 5697). The setup passes every `VITE_*` value on the command line and no dotfile was added.
- **Integration fixture conventions (step 20).** `test/integration/factories.ts` uses bound `INSERT` statements and `@test.lca` emails and creates sections through `saveSections`. The seed instead puts the JSON in `tournaments.sections` and lets the 0053 insert triggers build the section and schedule rows; the triggers never write `fee_early` or `fee_late`, so an `UPDATE` sets them. `test/unit/seed-fixtures.test.ts` proves it on a database built from 0001 to 0054 with `node:sqlite`. Its dry run of `db:seed:preview` rewrites the script, refuses to run unless the rewrite took, and runs it with a PATH that holds only a `wrangler` stub (exit 99) and a `node` wrapper that refuses any argument naming wrangler (exit 98), so a future form of the script can never reach the preview database from `npm test`.
- **Order of the web servers and `globalSetup` (step 20).** Confirmed: Playwright 1.63 starts the servers first (see Deviations, step 20).
- **Browser in this container (step 20).** Playwright 1.63.0 expects Chromium build 1243 and `/opt/pw-browsers` holds 1194; the suite ran with `PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` (see Deviations, step 20).
- **Sign-in with an unreachable Supabase (step 20).** Confirmed: signed-out pages make no Supabase call, and the smoke spec saw no request outside 127.0.0.1.
- **Package ages (step 20).** `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 was published Friday, September 4, 2026 and `@axe-core/playwright` 4.13.0 on Tuesday, August 11, 2026; both are over two weeks old at Tuesday, October 13, 2026.
- **The early stop's address check (step 20).** A first version of the Actions file's host check let `https://www.louisianachess.org./` and `https://someone:secret@louisianachess.org/` through (it printed that the preconditions were confirmed), and two tests in `e2e-preview-workflow.test.ts` failed. The check now reads the host with `new URL`; both addresses stop at the first job.
- **What `.dev.vars` did to the a11y servers (step 20).** A first version bound only the eight names in `.dev.vars.a11y`, so a developer's own `.dev.vars` still supplied the Stripe, Resend, Facebook and scanner-model keys. Fixed by the empty bindings (see the step).

- **The mapped classes on the plain `:root` (step 23).** `text-lca-navy` compiles to `var(--color-lca-navy)`, `#1a2744` in the brand `@theme` block, and `text-ink` to `var(--ink)`, `#1a2744` on the plain `:root`. `bg-white` compiles to `var(--color-white)`, `#fff`, which Tailwind's own `theme.css` defines, and `bg-surface` to `var(--surface)`, `#fff`. With a modifier both forms give the same `color-mix(in oklab, ...)` (see Deviations, step 23, for the fallback). The greys are not identical: `border-gray-300` is `oklch(87.2% 0.01 258.338)` against `--hairline` `oklch(0.922 0 0)`, and `bg-gray-100` `oklch(96.7% 0.003 264.542)` against `--surface-2` `oklch(0.97 0 0)`. Tailwind orders same-property utilities by name, so a rename moves where a class lands in the stylesheet; every element that pairs a renamed class with a rival of the same property does so inside `cn()`, whose `tailwind-merge` (3.6.0, which reads the new names as colours) keeps the last one by string order, or in branches of a ternary, so no winner changed.

Caslon has no tabular figures, which fits the rule that keeps it off ratings, scores and tables. `.small-caps` uses the uppercase fallback the brief gives, and `test/unit/heritage-glyphs.test.ts` holds both faces to having no smcp or c2sc.

Source Serif 4 Variable 5.3.0 calls its family `Source Serif 4 Variable`; `wght.css`, the same as `index.css`, declares six roman faces (cyrillic-ext, cyrillic, greek, vietnamese, latin-ext and latin, 181,072 bytes in all), `wght-italic.css` the same six in italic, and `opsz.css`, `opsz-italic.css`, `standard.css` and `standard-italic.css` the larger files. Kept as it was because acceptance criterion 4 asks for identical charges. It builds the hide key with `phaseKey(id, phase, round)`, passing the first round of the next playing day for `week` and `dayBefore` and the first round of that day for `checkin` and `eventDay`, so a strip hidden before day 1 comes back before round 2. Its `pollSeconds` rule (20 in `checkin`, `eventDay` and the round phases, 300 otherwise), the sooner-first sort and their tests are WS02's. When WS02 or WS07 changes the inputs, only `domain/events/eventMode.ts` and its test change. `eventPhase` can join the one-definition list in `test/unit/domain-shims.test.ts` once WS02 calls it, so a second copy fails the suite.

Both fail safe, nothing is written, but on a SQLite build that differs every section save would answer 409 (order) or 500 (error text) until the code changes. D1's version could not be read (`sqlite_version()` is blocked). Re-check when D1's engine changes; matching the older "JSON path error" wording is optional.

Bold and semibold text in the fallback take the regular face's numbers, though Georgia Bold is wider (an average width of 1062 against 913). Step 31 measured the swap where no Georgia is installed only: the swap of the faces on `/about` and `/governance/bylaws` is 0.0000 at 390 by 844 and 1280 by 800 pixels, light and dark, since the one element in a heritage face on those pages is the heading, whose line height its class fixes; the run with a face of Georgia's metrics was not made (see "The Georgia run (step 31)"), and the numbers are not tuned.
- **Hooks for the heritage pages (step 30).** The heritage type reaches only elements that carry its hooks. Step 31's `HeritageLayout` and the pages it wraps put `data-heritage="display"` on their h1 and h2 (through `PageHero` or the pages), `figure` on display figures such as "1915" and "300+", and `card`, `table` and `mat` on the boxes that take the 2px radius; WS14's bylaws and minutes reader puts `reader` on its text column; WS10's honour board heads take `.small-caps`. Body text outside a reader keeps the site's face until a step gives it a hook of its own. A page that sets `--display-size` sets it in rem or px or as a percentage, never as a bare number or in a unit of the heading's own font (the stylesheet's header says why, and `test/unit/heritage-css.test.ts` checks every value set under `src`). Step 31: the six pages' h1 take `display` through `PageHero`, their cards `card` and the Champions table's frame `table`, only inside the layout; no page shows a display figure, so `figure` waits for one, and `reader` and `.small-caps` wait for WS14 and WS10 (see "The hooks WS14 and WS10 put on (step 31)").
- **Georgia on the test computers (step 30).** Georgia is not installed on the computer that built this step, so a browser test there draws the device's serif while a heritage face loads, never the fallback faces. Step 31's layout shift check runs where Georgia is installed, or installs a face with Georgia's metrics for the test (Gelasio, which its designer made metrically compatible with Georgia, is one), and says which. Georgia is missing on many visitors' devices as well: Android phones, ChromeOS and most Linux systems have none, so there `local('Georgia')` finds nothing, both fallback faces are skipped, and the swap runs from the device's own serif (Noto Serif on Android), at its own size and metrics, to Caslon and Source Serif. The spec's budget is for a mid-tier phone (section 2.4, CLS under 0.1), so step 31 measures AC11 twice, once with a face that has Georgia's metrics and once with no Georgia, as an Android phone draws it. If the swap without Georgia is over 0.1, step 31 adds a second fallback face for each real face on Android's serif (`local('Noto Serif')`), its numbers worked out the same way, after the Georgia one in each stack. Step 31 made the second of the two runs only, with no Georgia on this computer, as an Android phone draws the page: the swap is 0.0000, so no second fallback face is added; no face with Georgia's metrics was installed or written for the test, and the first run is K's (see "The Georgia run (step 31)").
- **Source Serif 4 5.3.1 (step 30).** `@fontsource-variable/source-serif-4` 5.3.1 was published Sunday, October 11, 2026, and is two weeks old on Sunday, October 25, 2026. A later step may move to it then, with `npm install --save-exact`; `test/unit/heritage-budget.test.ts` and `test/unit/heritage-glyphs.test.ts` check its latin files' sizes and glyphs.
- **Letters outside the latin files (step 30).** Inside the heritage type a letter outside the latin files, in a Vietnamese or a Polish name for one, is drawn from Georgia or the device's serif, since only the latin files are named. Both packages ship a latin-ext file and Source Serif 4 a vietnamese one, which a browser would fetch only for such letters; step 31, WS10 (Champions) or WS14 (Board, Minutes) adds them if a name needs them.
- **The heritage stylesheet before the first paint (step 30).** `ThemeScope` asks for `src/styles/themes/heritage.css` in an effect, after the scope's first paint, and the file holds the font tokens, the type rules and the fallback faces as well as the faces (see Deviations, Step 30), so an element with a hook is drawn first in the base type and moves when the file arrives. A check in Chromium on the `a11y-on` build, served as files at 390 by 844 pixels with the stylesheet held back one second and the font files refused, so that no face could swap, and the hooks put on the fixture page's elements before its first paint: the h1 with the display hook painted at 30 pixels in Geist at 700 and became the Caslon stack at 36 pixels and 400 when the file arrived, a layout shift of 0.0145, and with a reading column of six paragraphs added the shift was 0.0964, nearly all of AC11's 0.1, before any face swapped. Step 31 loads the file before heritage content paints, and measures AC11 from the start of the navigation with the stylesheet held back as well as the faces, not only across the font swap. One way: `ThemeScope` keeps one promise of the import, which Vite's loader resolves once the stylesheet has loaded, and `HeritageLayout`'s lazy route waits for it. It must be the one promise, since Vite's loader answers a second request for a stylesheet it has already added at once, before the stylesheet has loaded, and a function exported beside the component draws the `react-refresh/only-export-components` lint warning, so the loader may need a module of its own, with the single-importer pins of `test/unit/theme-scope-wiring.test.ts` moved to it. That loader must also handle a failed load itself rather than call `import()` again, since Vite's loader answers a second request for a stylesheet that failed at once and fetches nothing, and leaves the failed `<link>` in the page (see Verify items, "The retry after a failed load (step 30)"). Two ways: take the failed `<link>` out and add a fresh one, its address from the file's `?url` import, or add one whose address carries a query that sets it apart from the one that failed. The live file has the same gap, which WS07 meets when it binds the live fonts; step 22's Fonts line, which says a failed import is retried by the next scope, holds for `ThemeScope`'s call and not for the file. The check in Chromium also found a shift that is not the look's: on a page the site loads on demand, the footer moves when the page takes the place of the loading line, a layout shift of 0.67 to 0.69 in all on `/about` and `/governance/bylaws` at 390 by 844 pixels and 0.22 to 0.35 at 1280 by 800, on both browser-test builds, so with `newLook` off as well, against 0.0057 to 0.0066 on `/`, which loads with the site (each `/api/` request answered 404). Step 31 keeps that shift apart from the look's, or holds the page's height while it loads, and says which. Done in step 31: `src/lib/scopeStylesheets.ts` keeps one promise per look and replaces a failed link with a fresh one carrying a query of its own, `HeritageLayout` waits for it with `ScopeStylesheetReady`, for three seconds at most, and the page's own arrival is measured apart from the swap; the layout's loading box holds the footer on a move inside the site (see the step).

Left as it is, since nothing fetches them. **Status:** in progress: nineteen steps in five checkpoints (E for steps 1 to 5, F for 6 to 8, G for 9 to 11, H for 12 to 16, I for 17 to 19); steps 1 to 9 are built.
**Branch:** `redesign/ws02-navigation`, cut from `main` at `34b721c`.
**PR:** draft pull request 110 carried checkpoint E (steps 1 to 5), merged into `main` as `8d7df98` on Friday, October 30, 2026; draft pull request 118 carried checkpoint F (steps 6 to 8), merged into `main` as `ed03823` on Sunday, November 1, 2026; checkpoint G (steps 9 to 11) comes in more than one pull request from this branch: draft pull request 119 carried WS02 step 9 alone, merged into `main` as `27fe278` on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, the checkpoint's later steps following in later pull requests from this branch.

- Read the brief with this path: the event-mode phase machine is `domain/events/eventMode.ts` (built in WS01, step 5), not `functions/utils/eventMode.ts`. `functions/api/me/event-mode.ts` imports `eventPhase`, `phaseKey` and `firstRoundTimesFromSchedule(schedule, date, endDate)` from it (`../../../domain/events/eventMode` from the server, `@domain/events/eventMode` in the site). The endpoint passes a round to `phaseKey` for `week` and `dayBefore` (the first round of the next playing day, 1 before day 1) and for `checkin` and `eventDay` (the first round of that day), because those phases come back on later days of a multi-day event and a key ending in `:0` would keep a hidden strip hidden. The endpoint, `src/lib/eventModeCopy.ts`, the strip, `pollSeconds` and the sooner-first sort are still WS02's. See the WS01 deviations "Event-mode phases (step 5)" and "Event-mode phase times (step 5)" (`eventDay` runs until 6:00 AM, not 11:59 PM) and the decision "Event-mode phase gaps (step 5)" (including days with no round).

Each step fills in its items when it lands. The map is a list and not a table, since the WS01 record tests read every table row in this file.

### WS02 step 1: the record, brief 1.4 and the stale-tab reload

The first step of checkpoint E, and of WS02. It records checkpoint D's merge, lands brief 1.4 as `docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md`, declares the eighteen switches of 1.4's flag table that `src/lib/features.ts` lacked, all off, opens this section with the map of what proves each criterion and decision, and adds one guard: a tab left open across a deploy reloads once on the build loader's event. It is records, switches and that guard. With the switches off, what a visitor sees changes only when one of the site's files fails to load: a stale tab now recovers by itself, and the bullet on the stale-tab reload, below, sets out what else its one reload in a tab changes.

Pull request 106 keeps its own copy of the spec at 1.3 and never carries 1.4.
- **The switches.** The eighteen switches of 1.4's flag table that `src/lib/features.ts` lacked follow `membershipRequirementSwitch`, in the table's order, under one section comment, each `false` with a one-line comment taken from its row of the table: `clubEmailHidden`, `rosterShortNames`, `newLive`, `resultReports`, `roundAlerts`, `followerAlerts`, `standingDirectors`, `tdConsole`, `adminHome`, `newClubs`, `newNews`, `newScholastic`, `seasonSchedule`, `newMembership`, `newDashboard`, `myLcaRail`, `newAbout` and `scanner2`. The file now declares 42, all off, and nothing reads the eighteen yet. - **The stale-tab reload.** On Thursday, October 22, K's admin tab of `/governance/minutes`, open since before checkpoint D's deploy, fell into the "Something went wrong" screen on "Add document": the code the tab had loaded named the editor's file by the content hash of its own build, and the new deployment no longer serves that file. A hard refresh mended it, and with a deploy for every checkpoint from now on it would happen to any tab left open. When a page's file, or a file it needs, fails to load, the build loader fires its own event, `vite:preloadError`, on `window`; the event can be cancelled, and the loader throws the error only when it is not. `src/lib/reloadOnStaleChunk.ts` listens for it, and `src/main.tsx` calls it before the app is drawn, outside the `newLook` block. The first time the event comes, the guard sets a mark in `sessionStorage` (`lca-stale-reload`), cancels the event and reloads the page once, which loads the new build. Once the mark is set it steps aside, so the error reaches the error screen as it does today and the page can never reload in a loop; the guard never clears the mark, which lasts as long as the tab. When storage cannot be read or written it steps aside as well, since it could not keep the reload to once. With the event cancelled, the loader's promise answers with nothing, so for an instant, while the reload begins, the page that asked for the file may fail on it and the error screen may show before the new page replaces it. A stylesheet the loader could not load is left alone: the looks' stylesheets, heritage's and live's, are the only ones a page asks for on demand, and `src/lib/scopeStylesheets.ts`, which asks for them, tries once more under a query of its own and then draws the page without the file, so such a failure never reached the error screen. The guard knows it by the loader's error, whose message begins "Unable to preload CSS", and neither cancels it nor spends the reload on it. The browser runs found this: the guard's first form answered those events too, and two tests of `test/a11y/heritage.spec.ts` ("the heritage stylesheet on its way") failed, since the page reloaded where it should have asked again under its query; with stylesheets left alone both pass. Two imports do not go through `lazy()`: a handler awaits each inside a try of its own, and the one reload comes before that handler's catch. They are the governance documents' file reader, `src/lib/parseDocumentFile.ts`, which `handleFile` in `src/areas/governance/components/GovernanceDocuments.tsx` imports when an admin picks a file for a document, and the scanner's decoder, which `src/lib/scanner/decodeInBackground.ts` imports only in a browser without Web Workers. On the first such failure in a tab the catch meets a TypeError, from reading the loader's answer, which is nothing, in place of the load error. An admin who picks a file in a stale tab sees an alert in that TypeError's words (in Chrome, "Cannot destructure property 'parseFileToHtml' of '(intermediate value)' as it is undefined."), perhaps only for a moment, where the alert named the load error before, and the reload then replaces the page, so the title and date typed into the open form are lost; before the guard they stayed, though no file could be read in that tab until it was refreshed. The scanner shows its own words as before ("The moves were read, but checking them failed. Please try again." or, when a move is fixed, "Couldn't update the game. Please try that move again."), and the reload then replaces the page and the scan it held. No switch governs the guard, and what a visitor sees changes only when a file fails to load, through its one reload in a tab: a stale tab mends itself, a page file that fails while the connection is down reloads the tab (see the judgement calls), and the two handlers above meet the reload as set out here. Since brief 1.4 lets nothing but what a screen reader hears ship with every switch off unless K says yes before the pull request merges (section 0.2 and Q34), the guard waits for K's yes before checkpoint E merges, or for a switch if K asks for one (see the follow-ups).

- **The signed-in visitor.** The test servers' sign-in address is a closed port (`http://127.0.0.1:9`), so nobody can sign in there, and the servers refuse every made-up token, as the role safety tests of `test/a11y/seeded-data.spec.ts` show. `test/a11y/signedIn.ts` draws a signed-in person in the browser instead:
  - Before the page loads it plants a session in the page's own `localStorage`, under the key the installed sign-in library reads for that address. The library builds the key from "sb-", the first part of the address's host name and "-auth-token", so for this address it is `sb-127-auth-token`, and the helper works it out from `FAKE_SUPABASE_URL` the same way. The session has the shape the library stores: an access token in three base64url parts, whose claims carry the assurance level (`aal1`, and `aal2` with a verified second factor for the two LCA admins, so the site does not send them to set one up); a refresh token; an end a day ahead; and the person's user record. It is planted only on the build's own address, only when the page holds no session, and only once in a tab (a mark in `sessionStorage`), so a test that logs out stays signed out on the pages it opens after.
  - It answers in the browser the five calls the site makes for a signed-in person: `POST /api/me` (201 and the member, the site's first call, which the plan's list leaves out), `GET /api/me` (the member, entries, events directed and children), `GET /api/board/my-seats` (seats and the clubs a regional seat covers), and `GET /api/me/event-mode` and `GET /api/live/now`, 204 with no body unless a person gives one. No page calls the last two yet; they come in WS02 steps 13 and 15. Every other call goes on to the local server with the planted token, which the server cannot check, so it answers a public call as for someone signed out and refuses a call that needs a sign-in.
  - It records and refuses every request the page makes to the fake sign-in address, and lists every call to the site's API answered 401, 403 or 500 and more, so a test can show none happened. `test/a11y/support.ts` tells local from outside by the host name alone, so it counts that address as local; the helper's own route, added after the support file's, is tried first.
  - What was found about the library (`@supabase/supabase-js` and its sign-in part, both 2.110.7): a stored session counts when it has an access token, a refresh token and an end; one that ends within 90,000 ms is refreshed through the sign-in service, and one that does not is read with no request at all; a stored session without its user record makes the library ask the service for the user, so the planted session carries one; and the assurance level comes from the token's claims and the user's verified factors, with no request. Measured: with the planted session no request went to the fake address on any page of the spec, and the session came back unchanged after a reload. Logging out sends one request there to end the session, which the helper refuses; the library removes the session all the same.
  - The race: the header shows Profile and Log out as soon as the session is read, before the member's answers arrive, and the More menu's account links need those answers (WS01's follow-up on the Admin link opened directly is a race of the same kind). So `waitForMemberAnswers` waits until `GET /api/me` and `GET /api/board/my-seats` have both been answered for the page open now, not for Profile. Every new page asks for the member again, so one call covers one page: the helper keeps the calls it answered for the page open now apart from all it answered, and empties that list when a new page takes the tab's main frame (a request for a document there, then the document itself), while a change of address the site makes without loading a page keeps it. A test that opens a second page calls the wait again, and the answers of the page before never let it return. `test/a11y/signed-in-edges.spec.ts` shows both, and against a wait that counts every answer since the sign-in it fails with "Received promise resolved instead of rejected".
  - The people, in `test/unit/fixtures/navPersonas.ts`, which `test/unit/nav.test.ts` reads under the unit tests and the browser tests read through the helper, so it imports nothing at run time (types only, which are erased): someone signed out; an active member (Riley Fixture); a member whose membership ends within 30 days; an expired member (Morgan Fixture); a parent of two (Dana Fixture, with Robin and Quinn); the director of one event; a club rep; a regional representative (Jordan Fixture, with the seed's regional seat and its club); an LCA officer (Avery Fixture, with the seed's officer seat); the president; an LCA admin; and one person holding everything a person can hold at once (an LCA admin with a second factor, two children, an event they direct, an officer seat and a regional seat with its club; a person has one role, so a club rep cannot also be an admin). Each carries the bodies of the five answers, what the My LCA rows read, and the account links today's More menu shows them. The five the seed already holds are the seed's people in full, with their names and memberships and with the seed's children, seats and entries for them (Avery Fixture's entries in the Fixture Fall Open and the finished Fixture Summer Championship, Jordan, Morgan and Riley Fixture's in the second, and Dana Fixture's children's in the first), so a later test that asks the real server about one of them gets what the list gives; `test/unit/nav-personas-edges.test.ts` and `test/integration/nav-personas.test.ts` compare the children, seats and entries both ways. Every person, address, club and event is made up, in the seed's style, and the dates are worked out from the day the list is made for.

- **The browser bar colour.** Under `newLook`, once a visitor picks Light or Dark, the page's `theme-color` is that look's, `#1a2744` for Light and `#0b1220` for Dark, whatever the device says; with System, `index.html`'s two metas, one for a light device and one for a dark one, follow the device as before. A browser takes the first `theme-color` meta in the page whose media matches the device or that has none, so a pick adds one meta of its own, with no media and the look's colour, first in the head, where it wins over the two, and System takes it away. `PREPAINT_SCRIPT` adds it before the first paint: the script runs at the very top of the head, before the parser has reached `index.html`'s metas, so it could not change those two and adds its own instead, in a try of its own after the class and `data-look`, so a head it cannot reach never costs the dark class. `createColorScheme` keeps the same meta afterwards: it finds the one the choice owns by its attribute, `data-appearance`, brings its colour up to date, moves it first if it is not, removes any second one, adds it for Light or Dark when it is missing and removes it for System; it does nothing when `newLook` is off or when it is handed no head, and a head that throws leaves the dark class right. The two colours are exported constants of `src/lib/colorScheme.ts`, `THEME_COLOR_LIGHT` and `THEME_COLOR_DARK`, which the script, the module and `test/unit/theme-color.test.tsx` share, and the test holds `index.html`'s two metas to them. The module still reads no browser global: `src/hooks/useColorScheme.ts` hands it the page's head, as it hands it the root. The script is 543 characters, 258 more than before, and the page's charset meta still ends inside its first 1,024 bytes, with 388 to spare.
- **The chrome's rings.** Under `newLook`, rules in `src/index.css` after the older ring rules set the ring's colour for the chrome by an attribute of its own, `data-ring-ground`: `navy` on the chrome's navy grounds (the header, the phone's app bar, the round-state strip and the footer) gives the gold ring, `#c8a94a`; `light` on a light surface they open (the About and My LCA menus, the Menu sheet and drawer, the search panel) gives the look's own ring back, the navy `#1a2744` in the light look and `#c8a94a` in dark mode, where that surface is navy; and `gold` on an opaque gold ground gives the navy ring in both modes. Each sets `--focus`, the colour the one ring is drawn in, which every control inside takes, so a light surface inside a navy one gets its own ring by its own attribute. The colours are written as hex, the values of `--gold-on-dark` and the brand navy, as every `--focus` of the new look is (`test/unit/tokens.test.ts` holds them so), and the dark mode rule sits inside `@media screen`, like the dark tokens. No element of the site carries `navy` or `light` yet: WS02 steps 5 to 8 put them on the header, the bars, the menus, the sheet and the footer as each is built. The older navy band rule (`.bg-lca-navy`, `.bg-brand-navy` and `[data-ground="dark"]`, each with its menu exception) stays exactly as it was for the page heroes; it sets the ring's colour outright and wins over `--focus`, so no chrome surface may sit inside one of those classes (see the follow-ups). `test/unit/contrast.test.ts` reads each ring as a browser works it out and holds every pair to 3:1 or more: gold on the navy chrome, `#1a2744`, 6.51:1 in both modes; navy on a light surface's white, on the sheet's row `#fbfaf6` and on the About menu's current row `#f3eedc` in the light look; gold on dark mode's navy surface and on a row with a tenth of white over it; and navy on the banners' gold in both modes, 6.51:1, where dark mode's own ring would be gold on gold, 1:1. The round-state strip is drawn in the live look, whose ring the looks block of that file already holds to 3:1 on its grounds, so it needs no pair of its own.
- **The banners' ring.** `AnnouncementBanner`'s gold tone, and a tone it does not know, which it draws gold, carry `data-ring-ground="gold"` on the element that holds the link and the dismiss button, and `ImpersonationBanner` carries it on its root, around the Exit button. Under `newLook` their controls' ring is navy on the gold in the light look and in dark mode, where it was gold on the gold. Neither banner's classes change, and `data-ground` stays `dark` on the urgent and info tones and absent on the gold, navy and unknown ones, so the pins of `test/unit/semantic-map-grounds.test.ts` and `test/unit/semantic-map.test.ts` hold as they were. This is the one place in this step where a visitor with only `newLook` on sees a ring change; with `newLook` off the marker changes nothing, which `test/a11y/nav.spec.ts` measures on `a11y-off`. The seed holds no announcement and no one is viewed as another, so the browser spec stubs the announcement and plants the impersonation target.
- **The skip link and the loading line.** With the chrome on, `src/App.tsx` draws "Skip to content" as the first child of the page's frame, before the impersonation banner, the announcement banner and the header, so it is the first thing Tab reaches at every width. It is hidden until it has the focus, then drawn fixed at the top left of the window above the header, on a ground of its own (`bg-raised` with `text-ink`, white and navy in the light look, navy and near white in dark mode), with its ring drawn 4 pixels inside its edge (`outline-offset: -4px`), so the line has the link's own ground on both sides wherever it shows: over the navy header, over a gold banner or over the page. It points at `#main-content`, the main's id, and a click moves the focus there and keeps `#main-content` out of the address, while the link still works in a browser that runs no script. The main takes `tabindex="-1"` from that click and gives it back as soon as the focus leaves it, so it is never a stop of its own and a click on a page's text never puts the focus on it; a main that held it always did, and the next Tab then began at the main's top rather than after what was clicked, which the run of the specs that press Tab found (see the verify item on them). The main, a landmark and not a control, draws no ring when it takes the focus. The loading line keeps its status role, its spinner and its words "Loading…", and holds the height of the window under the header (`min-h-[calc(100vh-var(--header-h,64px))]`) with today's row at its top; `--header-h` does not exist until WS02 step 5, so its 64 pixels stand in for it, and today's 65-pixel header only makes the line a pixel taller than it needs to be. The line also carries `data-loading-line`, and while it shows the footer is not drawn: one rule of `src/index.css`, `:root[data-look="new"] main:has(> [data-loading-line]) + footer`, sets it to `display: none`, outside every layer, so the footer comes with the page. The height alone keeps the footer below the window while the code comes, which is enough on a page taller than the window; on a page shorter than it, the footer then rose into view as the page came, a shift of its own: on `/donate/success`, where a donor comes back from the payment page, 0.2566 at 390 pixels and 0.1622 at 1280 with the rule turned off, against 0.1115 and 0.0001 with every switch off. With the footer not drawn until the page is there, `/donate/success` shifts 0.0000 and 0.0001, as `test/a11y/nav.spec.ts` holds, and the brief's two pages as before. A browser that does not know `:has()` drops the rule and draws the footer under the tall line, as before the rule. With the chrome off nothing of this is drawn: the main is `<main class="flex-1">` and the loading line is today's markup, byte for byte, as `test/unit/app-frame.test.tsx` holds with every switch off, with `newNav` on alone and with `newLook` on alone. The condition is read by calling `chromeOn` as the page is drawn, not when the module loads; `src/App.tsx` gains no `lazy()` and does not name the scope component.

- **Judgement calls.** K reviews these:
  - The browser bar's colour comes from a meta of the module's own, first in the head and owned afterwards by the colour scheme code, rather than from changing `index.html`'s two, which the script cannot reach before they are parsed; what is held is the page's colour as a browser works it out. The notes for this workstream accept this.
  - The meta the choice owns is marked `data-appearance`, holding the look it was added for, so nothing ever touches `index.html`'s two.
  - The chrome's rings are set by `data-ring-ground`, an attribute of their own, not by `data-ground`, which the grounds tests allow in four files and read as a dark ground whatever its value.
  - The rings set `--focus` and never `outline-color`, so the tests that look up the one rule with each outline colour still find the band rule, and a light surface inside a navy one gets its ring from its own attribute.
  - The ring colours are written as hex, as every `--focus` of the new look is, rather than as `var(--gold-on-dark)` and `var(--color-brand-navy)`.

Nothing else changes, its four raw colour classes, its Facebook link and its two Log in links among them. `test/unit/fixtures/navbar-today.tsx` is the file as it stood at `7568680`, made with `cp`, with its first comment and its export's name changed and nothing else; `test/unit/header-today.test.tsx` draws the two under the same router and sign-in and compares their markup byte for byte, closed, with the More menu opened by a click and with the drawer opened as well: the live header's is the copy's once every `aria-current="page"` is taken out, and `aria-current="page"` sits on exactly the links today's rule marks, never on the brand link, Profile, Log in or Join LCA. In the browser on `a11y-off` it sits on Clubs in the bar on `/clubs` at 1280 pixels, on Support in the More menu on `/support`, on Clubs in the drawer at 390, and on nothing on `/`.
- **The header and its brand link.** `SiteHeader` draws one `<header>`, the page's banner, `data-slot="site-header"`, sticky at the top with `z-50` under the skip link, 64 pixels high (`h-16`) with no border, on the brand navy through its variable, `bg-(--color-brand-navy)`, rather than `.bg-brand-navy`, `.bg-lca-navy` or `data-ground`, so the navy band rule, whose gold ring outranks the menus' own, reaches neither panel; `data-ring-ground="navy"` gives its controls the gold ring (WS02 step 3's rule). The row is `max-w-6xl` with 24 pixels a side and a 16-pixel gap. The brand link to `/` is named "Louisiana Chess Association, home" by `aria-label`, whatever is shown: `LcaMark` at 30 pixels with an empty title, hidden from screen readers, on no plate, then the two-line name, "Louisiana Chess" over "Association", in the header's white; the header draws no image and no gold words. As measured at 1024, 1280 and 1440 by 800: one banner, 64 pixels high on `rgb(26, 39, 68)`, the mark first in the link with `aria-hidden="true"` on a clear ground, every part of the row inside the header, each after the one before it and on one line, nothing wider than the window, and after a 600-pixel scroll the header still at the top and 64 pixels high.
- **The sections.** `<nav aria-label="Main">` holds the six sections from `headerSections()` in `src/lib/nav.ts`, in their order: Tournaments, Clubs, Scholastic, News, Membership and About, five links and About's button, each 15 pixels at weight 500, 12 pixels a side and 44 high. The section a page is in, by `sectionFor`, carries `aria-current="page"` and a 2-pixel line of the gold for dark grounds at its foot, drawn as a shadow inside its box, so no box changes as the page changes; a hover draws a 1-pixel line of the words' white in the same place, never a veil. As measured at 1280 pixels: the line, `rgb(200, 169, 74) 0px -2px 0px 0px inset`, on Tournaments, Clubs, Scholastic, News, Membership and About on `/tournaments`, `/clubs`, `/scholastic`, `/news`, `/membership` and `/governance/minutes`, nothing on `/`, and every section's box the same on each page. In forced colours, the mode a contrast theme on Windows draws pages in, no shadow is drawn, so there the current section is underlined instead, 2 pixels thick, in the colour the person's own palette gives words, and a section under the pointer is underlined too; an underline changes no box either, and outside forced colours no section is underlined. As measured at 1280 pixels in forced colours: no shadow drawn, Tournaments underlined on `/tournaments` and About on `/governance/minutes`, no section on `/`, Clubs underlined under the pointer, every section's box as on `/`, and Tournaments drawn otherwise on its own page than on `/` and the same on `/governance/minutes`, so the underline is drawn, not only written.
- **The About menu.** About ▾ is a disclosure: a button with `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` naming its panel while the panel is drawn, which it is only while open, and no `aria-haspopup`. Its rows come from `aboutMenu()` in `src/lib/nav.ts`: About LCA (`/about`); Board & regions, Bylaws & rules and Minutes (`/governance/board`, `/governance/bylaws` and `/governance/minutes`, then `/about/board`, `/about/bylaws` and `/about/minutes` once `newAbout` is on); Annual meeting (`/meeting`); State champions (`/champions`, then `/about/champions` once `newNews` is on); Contact (`/contact`); then, below a line, "LCA on Facebook ↗", the association's Facebook page in a new tab. Its keys, which `useNavMenu` in `src/components/layout/navMenu.ts` gives the My LCA menu too: a click, Enter and Space show or hide it; ArrowDown opens it on its first row and ArrowUp on its last; inside, the arrow keys move from row to row and wrap, Home and End go to the first and the last; Esc closes it and gives the focus back to About; Tab goes on in the page's order and the menu closes once the focus has left it; a press or a touch outside it, choosing a row and a change of page close it; nothing opens it on hover. The current row is the one row whose address the path is at or under, the longest when several are, so About LCA only when no other row is: with `newAbout` and `newNews` on, Board & regions alone on `/about/board` and State champions alone on `/about/champions`. It carries `aria-current="page"` and "You are here" beside its title, hidden from screen readers, since `aria-current` says it to them. The panel is `bg-raised` with `text-ink`, a hairline border and `data-ring-ground="light"`, so its rows take the look's own ring. As measured on `/governance/minutes` at 1280 pixels: Minutes the current row, "You are here" `rgb(112, 87, 24)` on `rgb(243, 238, 220)` at 13 pixels and weight 600 on a white panel in the light look, and in the menu's ink on its own row on a `rgb(26, 39, 68)` panel in dark mode.

While the session itself is read, Log in and Join LCA show, as today's header shows them. As measured: `/tournaments?when=weekend#list` handed whole, in the history entry's `usr`; Join LCA signed out, nothing for an active member and for one whose membership ends in 20 days, and for an expired member nothing while the member's answers are held, then Renew, last in the row, on `rgb(200, 169, 74)` with `rgb(26, 39, 68)` words, opening `/membership`. The sign-in context holds no children yet, so the Family row waits for WS02 step 17, and the Membership card for `newMembership`. As drawn on `a11y-on`: My LCA and Log out for an active member, Workspace between them for the director of an event, and Board inbox and Admin for an LCA admin; Log out from the menu's last row, by the keyboard, signs the person out and opens `/`, where Log in is back.
- **Donate.** `src/components/DonateButton.tsx` now exports `DonateDialog`, the dialog its caller opens and closes, and `DonateButton`, the dialog with today's trigger, the outline button with the heart, as it was drawn; the dialog's words and fields are as they were. With `newMembership` off the header's Donate opens the dialog, from the bar and, once the row is tight, from the About menu's Donate row, one dialog drawn by the header, the focus going back to what opened it, or to About once the row has gone; with `newMembership` on Donate is a link to `/give`. The dialog's own code is fetched the first time Donate is pressed, not with the header (the dialog parts it shares with the scanner page come with that page, as the Build bullet says): `SiteHeader` loads `DonateDialog` with `lazy()`, draws it inside `Suspense` from the first press on and keeps it drawn, closed, after that, so it closes as it did and gives the focus back; a tab left open across a deploy reloads once on that first press, as it does for a page's file (WS02 step 1). The dialog hands the donor to Stripe's checkout in the same tab with `window.location.assign`, as the membership and household checkouts do, and stays on "Starting checkout…" until the page leaves; a donor the browser's Back button brings back gets the button back. A donor who closes the dialog while the checkout is asked for, by Esc, its close button or a press outside it, has changed their mind: when the answer comes the tab stays where it is, and the dialog opened again has its amount and its button back, with no message from a checkout that failed meanwhile; the same when the dialog leaves the page, as it does when the window narrows below 1024 pixels. Each press of Continue to payment asks afresh. It used to open the checkout with `window.open` once the request came back, which browsers, phones above all, block when it does not come straight from the tap, so nothing happened. No page drew the dialog before this step, and none draws it with the chrome off. As measured: Donate in the bar opens "Support the Louisiana Chess Association", drawn once, and Esc closes it with nothing sent and the focus back on Donate; with the checkout held, Esc closed the dialog, the tab stayed on `/` when the answer came, the dialog opened again with 25 and Continue to payment, and a second press moved the tab to the payment page.
- **The squeeze.** `SiteHeader` keeps a level: 0, everything in the bar; 1, Donate as the About menu's last row, above the Facebook row; 2, the two-line name hidden as well, the link keeping its name. A ResizeObserver over the row and every part whose width can change (the name, the sections, Donate and the account) works out the room inside the row's padding and each level's natural width, a sum of the parts' widths and the row's gaps, keeping the widths Donate and the name had when last drawn, so a level's natural width does not change with the level; the first level that fits is taken, which depends on the room alone and cannot flap at its edge. No section, Log in or My LCA, Join LCA or Renew ever leaves the bar, and when even level 2 does not fit the row stays at it. The widest row as measured on `a11y-on`, on `/` with its fonts in: the room is 976 pixels at 1024 and 1,104 at 1280 and 1440, the row's 1,152 less its padding; the mark is 30 pixels, the name 126.9, the six sections 538.3, Donate 63, Log in and Join LCA 153.3 with their gap, My LCA 86.2 alone and 169.6 with Renew. Signed out the natural widths are 959.5, 892.5 and 753.6 for levels 0, 1 and 2, so level 0 with 16.5 pixels to spare at 1024 and 144.5 at 1280 and 1440; as an active member 892.4, 825.4 and 686.5, level 0 with 83.6 and 211.6 to spare; as an expired member 975.8, 908.8 and 769.9, level 0 with 0.2 to spare at 1024 and 128.2 at 1280 and 1440. Search's button, 112 pixels on the decided board, and the row's 16-pixel gap would add 128: at 1024 the row would take level 2 signed out (94.4 to spare) and as an expired member (78.1), and level 1 as an active member (22.6); at 1280 and 1440 it would keep level 0 (16.5, 83.6 and 0.2 to spare). The Live tag, 50 pixels by the board's spare figures, beside Search would put 1280 and 1440 at level 1 signed out (33.5) and as an expired member (17.2), keep the active member at level 0 (33.6), and leave 1024 at level 2 (44.4, 111.5 and 28.1). Both steps are shown in `test/a11y/nav.spec.ts` at 1024 by 800, the row made tighter a pixel of letter spacing at a time on the name, the window and the header's height unchanged: Donate leaves the bar for the About menu's last row, where it opens the same dialog, then the name hides, never the other way round and never back while the row stays tight. The browser runs hide the scrollbar, so the 1024 figures above are for a window with none: a classic scrollbar of 15 to 17 pixels on a page taller than the window leaves the row 959 to 961 pixels of room at 1024, which puts an expired member at level 1 and a signed-out visitor at the edge of level 0. The squeeze is measured live, so the code adapts, and WS02 step 18 starts from these figures.

- **The widths.** `src/hooks/useWideScreen.ts` answers two lines, each from the browser's own media query through `useSyncExternalStore`, so a bar is drawn on the first paint and swaps the moment the window crosses a line: `WIDE_QUERY`, `(min-width: 1024px)`, with `useWideScreen`, as before, and `TABLET_QUERY`, `(min-width: 768px)`, with `useTabletScreen`, its sibling, one small factory giving each query its subscription and its answers. Where `matchMedia` is missing, as in the unit tests that draw the whole app, and when drawn to a string, both answer false, so the app bar is drawn. `ChromeHeader` in `src/components/layout/Navbar.tsx` asks both on every draw and draws `SiteHeader` in its desktop form from 1024 pixels up, the same element in its tablet form from 768 to 1023, and `MobileAppBar` below; `Navbar` still chooses the chrome before any hook runs, and with either switch off it draws today's header at every width.

In order: the brand link named "Louisiana Chess Association, home", the rook at 30 pixels hidden from screen readers and the two-line name; `<nav aria-label="Main">` with Tournaments and Clubs alone, the first two sections, the current one with `aria-current="page"` and the gold line at its foot; Donate, opening today's donation dialog in one click (a link to `/give` with `newMembership` on), which never leaves the bar; Log in or the My LCA menu; and the bordered Menu button, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and, while the drawer is open, `aria-controls` naming it, which opens the Menu sheet as the drawer. There is no Join slot in the tablet form, since the sheet holds Join LCA and Renew, and no tab bar. The two-line name is the row's one give: the squeeze keeps its levels, but in the tablet form Donate counts at every level, so the row goes from everything in the bar straight to the name hidden, the link keeping its name. As the window widens into the desktop form the drawer closes, since that form has no Menu button to come back to. - **The Menu sheet.** `MobileMenu` is a modal dialog named Menu on the site's dialog primitive: `src/components/ui/dialog.tsx` gives its root, portal, scrim (`data-slot="menu-sheet-scrim"`, `bg-black/50`), title and close control as they are, and the content is the primitive's own, since the wrapper's `DialogContent` is a centred box with a close button of its own, so the sheet sets its own classes on the bare content, `aria-describedby={undefined}` among them so no description is asked for. The content carries `data-slot="menu-sheet"`, `data-shape` and `data-ring-ground="light"`, on `bg-raised` with `text-ink`, a column the height of the window in one of two shapes from the bar that opens it: `full` from the app bar, the window's own box, and `drawer` from the tablet header, 400 pixels wide against the window's right edge and its full height, with a hairline on its left, over the scrim. Its top bar holds the close control first, a bordered button showing an icon and the word Close and named "Close menu", then the title, Menu. The primitive keeps the focus inside the sheet, closes it on Esc and on a press outside it (the scrim beside the drawer), hides the page behind it from assistive technology and keeps that page from scrolling; the sheet opens with the focus on "Close menu" and, as it closes, gives the focus back to the Menu button that opened it, both moves made without scrolling the page, so the reader keeps their place. Following a row closes it, and so does a change of page, which the bar that holds it sees. Its rows sit inside `ScrollPanel`, named "Sections and links", a region in the tab order, with the panel's bound, border and rounding taken off by its classes, so the list scrolls inside the sheet while the page behind stays still (D16). As measured: at 390 by 844 the sheet's box is the window's, and at 768 by 1024 and 1023 by 800 the drawer is 400 pixels wide, its right edge at the window's, the window's full height, the scrim over the whole window; Tab from its last control, Dark, comes back to "Close menu" and Shift+Tab goes back; Esc and the close control each close it, and a press on the scrim closes the drawer, each time with the focus on Menu; in a window 390 by 480 on a touch screen, with About open, the list scrolls by Page Down, End and Home on its region and by a finger's drag, sent as the touch events a touch screen sends, the wheel not used, while the page behind stays where it was, 300 pixels down, before, during and after, and a drag on the sheet's own bar moves nothing.

A row whose address is not live is not drawn. With the `a11y-on` build's switches the sheet holds no This weekend, Results or Suggest a club, and the About rows open today's addresses; with `newTournaments`, `newNews` and `newClubs` on those three rows join, and with `myLcaRail` on the Admin row is the one role row. As drawn on `a11y-on` at 390 pixels on `/clubs`, signed out: the six sections, Clubs open with "You are here" and All clubs marked as the page, the others shut, the buttons Donate, Log in and Join LCA, no account rows, the three links, and Tournaments, once opened, holding All tournaments and Scoresheet scanner; signed in, the buttons Donate and My LCA, with Renew beside them for an expired member, and the account rows Log out for an active member and an expired one, Workspace and Log out for the director of one event, and Board inbox, Admin and Log out for an LCA admin.

The control takes two props: `labelId`, `appearance-label` by default, which the sheet gives an id of its own from `useId`, so the page never holds one id twice; and `on`, the ground it is drawn on, `navy` by default, the footer's, and `light` for the sheet, the name the site's components drawn on both grounds use. Its white words, borders and veil are drawn under the literal condition `on === 'navy'`, so `test/unit/semantic-map-grounds.test.ts`'s veil test passes as it did; the light form draws its label in the sheet's ink at weight 600 and its buttons 44 pixels high, the pressed one marked by the ink's line, the muted fill and weight 600 beside `aria-pressed`. The footer's control keeps its markup, its classes and its id, byte for byte. As measured on `a11y-on` at 390 pixels: with the sheet open the one group named Appearance found is the sheet's, since the page behind is hidden from assistive technology; Dark picked there sets the page's dark class and the browser bar's colour as the footer's control does, the footer's shows Dark once the sheet has closed, and a pick of System in the footer shows in the sheet the next time it opens.

It draws nothing at all from 768 pixels up, on the pages that hide the tab bar, while the keyboard is open and in the reflow fallback. `DockProvider`, around the whole page frame, holds what the bars, the tab bar and the dock share (`src/components/layout/dockParts.ts`): the one Menu sheet, its id, its opener and the way back for the focus, whether the tab bar is drawn now, and the bars a page puts in the dock. A page's bar is a `DockBar` of kind `action` or `event`, drawn into its place while the dock draws it, and nothing otherwise; the dock counts the bars of each kind in a store `DockBar` joins before the first paint, and while an event bar is drawn the action bar's place is not, one contextual bar at a time. No page draws a `DockBar` yet: `test/unit/bottom-dock.test.tsx` draws one of each kind, and `test/a11y/dock.spec.ts` plants a bar 64 pixels tall in the action place, which the dock measures like any bar.

Each tab is the whole cell, at least 44 by 44 pixels, an icon over its label, the label always shown: 80 pixels wide at 320, 90 at 360 and 97.5 at 390, its words at 12 pixels and weight 500, 11 pixels under 360 (the replan's line 290: "Tournaments" is 66.8 pixels of its 80 at 320, at 11 pixels, and 72.9 of 90 at 360, at 12). Measured in the browser, the words are 14.81:1 on the white in the light look, and in dark mode 14.68:1 for the current tab's and 7.10:1 for the others' muted ink; the bar is 5.13:1 on the white and 7.64:1 on the dark surface. A press on Tournaments, Clubs or Log in beside the open sheet lands outside it the same way, so it only closes the sheet, and the tab is followed on a second press; the browser tests measure the press on Close, and K looks at the others on a phone. - **The footer.** `SiteFooter`, which `Footer` in `src/components/layout/Footer.tsx` draws with the chrome on at every width, is one `<footer data-slot="site-footer" data-ring-ground="navy">`, the page's `contentinfo`, on the brand navy read through its variable, `bg-(--color-brand-navy)`, `#1a2744` in every look, with a 3 pixel line of brand gold along its top, kept out of print. With every switch off in the model its four columns are Play: Tournaments (`/tournaments`), Scholastic (`/scholastic`), State champions (`/champions`) and Scoresheet scanner (`/scanner`); Community: Clubs (`/clubs`), Club map (`/clubs#map`), List or update your club (`/contact?subject=club`), News (`/news`) and LCA on Facebook ↗, the association's Facebook page in a new tab; About LCA: About LCA (`/about`), Board & regions (`/governance/board`), Bylaws & rules (`/governance/bylaws`), Minutes (`/governance/minutes`) and Annual meeting (`/meeting`); and Contact: `LouisianaChess@gmail.com`, a `mailto:` link with a mail icon hidden from screen readers, Contact (`/contact`), Membership help (`/contact?subject=membership`), Website help (`/support`) and Donate, a button that opens the donation dialog. `newTournaments` adds Calendar (`/tournaments?view=calendar`) to Play; `newNews` adds Results (`/results`) to Play and moves State champions to `/about/champions`; `newClubs` adds Suggest a club (`/clubs/suggest`) to Community; `newAbout` moves Board & regions, Bylaws & rules and Minutes to `/about/board`, `/about/bylaws` and `/about/minutes`, in the columns and the trust line alike; and `newMembership` makes Donate a link to `/give`. Every link and button is an entry by id, its words the entry's one label and its address the entry's, and `SiteFooter.tsx` names no label, address or column of its own, as `test/unit/footer.test.tsx` holds against its source. The links are white, underlined on hover and when focused, 44 pixels high below 768 pixels and 34 from there up, and a word too long for its line, the address in a narrow column, breaks rather than spill. Measured in the browser on `/`, the footer is 971 pixels tall at 390 as it starts, the dock's 57 pixel room under its last line included, and 1,617 with every list open; 852 at 768 and 826 at 1023, where the four columns sit two by two under the brand block; and 397 at 1024 and 386 at 1280, where the brand block and the four columns share one row.
- **The brand block and the logo.** First at every width and never folded: the official logo, `LcaLogo` with its `sized` prop at 56 by 56 pixels and empty words, on no plate, beside "Louisiana Chess Association" in words, white, 17 pixels at weight 700, so the logo's own words are empty; the board's sentence, "Tournaments, clubs and scholastic chess across the state, run by volunteers.", 14 pixels in white at 80 per cent; and the join slot beside Donate, a grid of two 48 pixel buttons below 768 pixels and two 40 pixel buttons in a row from there up. The join slot follows the header's rule, `headerUtilities` and `joinSlotOf`: Join LCA for a visitor signed out and for someone signed in with no membership, Renew once a membership has expired, and nothing for an active member or while the member loads, drawn as the header draws it, the gold `Button` round a router link to `/membership`; Donate is outlined in white on the navy. The block is not a link. `npm run images` makes the two sized files from `src/assets/lca-logo.webp` with `sharp` at quality 90, the ratio kept, beside their source: `src/assets/lca-logo-56.webp`, 56 by 56 pixels and 1,818 bytes, sha256 `5c1992cc7ae3e4cc3e3fefc2ce45e862df2112a273f9f0070051951b85437ec3`, and `src/assets/lca-logo-112.webp`, 112 by 112 pixels and 4,596 bytes, sha256 `845e5220835af0faf4cc95f7d9546595fc876ce119cb1364783449292db3137f`, both lossy WebP, the same bytes on a second run, and the hero's 30 files unchanged. `LcaLogo`'s props are a union, so `sized` is taken only with a width and a height of 56: the image then holds the 56 pixel file at 1x and the 112 pixel file at 2x in its `srcset`, with the 400-pixel file as its `src`, and without it the image is today's, byte for byte. `vite.config.ts`'s `assetsInlineLimit` is `inlineAsset`, which answers `false` for the two files, so neither is ever written into a script, and leaves every other asset to the default limit. In the browser at 1280 by 800 on `/`, the footer's logo takes the 56 pixel file at a density of 1, 1,818 bytes fetched, its natural size 56 by 56, and the 112 pixel file at a density of 2, 4,596 bytes, its frame header 112 by 112, where the 400-pixel file is 16,468: 14,650 and 11,872 bytes fewer, against WS01 step 29's lab check's "about 15 KB" a page. No response on `/` carries the 400-pixel file's bytes at either density, and `/about`'s own 160-pixel logo still fetches it.
- **The build date and the trust line.** The trust line, `<ul aria-label="About this site">`, holds five items: "US Chess state affiliate", "Louisiana's chess community since 1915", Bylaws & rules and Minutes, the two entries of `TRUST_LINE_LINKS`, and "Site last updated" with the build's date in a `<time>` whose `dateTime` is the instant, its words the Louisiana day with its weekday and year through `formatDate`, `Sat, Oct 31, 2026` for `2026-10-31T14:42:00.000Z` and `Fri, Oct 30, 2026` for `2026-10-31T03:00:00.000Z`, the evening before in Louisiana. From 768 pixels up a middle dot stands between the items, hidden from screen readers; below that each item is a line of its own, with no dot. The date is the build's date, which the plugin writes into the page at build time: `prepaintPlugin` in `vite.config.ts` works out the instant once per build, `new Date().toISOString()`, UTC whatever the machine's zone, and with the chrome on in the build writes one `<meta name="build-date">` right after the viewport tag, through `withBuildDate` beside `withCoverViewport`, the build stopping unless the page holds that tag once; with either switch off it writes nothing, and the built `index.html` is today's. Only a build with the chrome on writes it, and the date is the build's, not the commit's: the CI build and the Pages build each run at their own time and each writes its own. `index.html` is never hashed, so nothing is renamed for the date, and no script holds the build's instant. `lastUpdated()` in `src/components/layout/footerParts.ts` answers nothing for a page with no meta or a meta that holds no instant, and the trust line then has no date. In the browser on `a11y-on` the drawn `<time>` holds the page's meta, an instant no later than the test's own now, and its words are that instant's Louisiana day, worked out in the test with `America/Chicago`.

- **The listing rule.** `functions/utils/events/listing.ts` exports one function, `listedWhere(alias)`, which gives today's rule for the alias it is handed, `t.is_visible = 1` for `listedWhere('t')`, as a piece of SQL for a prepared statement's WHERE clause, and throws for an alias that is not a plain name (a letter or an underscore, then letters, digits and underscores), so nothing but a table's name or alias is written into a query through it. It is the SQL fragment alone, with no Drizzle form, since every read of the search is a prepared statement on `context.env.DB`, as the clearinghouse feed's are. `test/unit/listing-rule.test.ts` reads the text of the files whose public queries of `tournaments` are held to the rule, `functions/api/search.ts` and `functions/utils/search.ts`, and fails when one of them names the column at all, comments included, or holds a SQL text that reads `tournaments`, under any alias, without `listedWhere` called inside the same text; it reads the rule's home apart (it exports `listedWhere`, writes the condition once, gives the two fragments and refuses six aliases), and runs its check over planted sources: one that writes the condition itself fails, one that takes it from `listedWhere` passes, and one that reads `tournaments` with neither fails, in a plain string, a template and a join; 18 cases in all. `test/unit/listing-rule-edges.test.ts` holds the rule closer: each read of `tournaments` in the two files hands `listedWhere` the very name it reads the table under, as a term of its `WHERE` clause joined by `AND`, never after `OR`, never under `NOT` and never among the columns read. The seven older public queries that write the rule themselves are left as they are, for WS03's shared event query: `functions/api/tournaments.ts` 40 and 46, `functions/api/clearinghouse.ts` 48, `functions/api/champions.ts` 14 and 20, `functions/api/clubs/[id].ts` 38 and `functions/tournaments/[id].ts` 36, with the rule written in code at `functions/api/tournaments/[id].ts` 24, as the follow-up names them. No index and no migration: WS02 adds none, and the tables are small.
- **The normaliser.** `domain/format/searchText.ts`, importing nothing, holds `normalizeSearchText`, which reads text as search compares it, in this order: small letters; the marks taken off the letters, once each letter is split from its marks, so "Café" reads "cafe" and "İstanbul" "istanbul"; "&" read as "and"; every run of what is not a letter or a digit read as one space, so punctuation, dashes, apostrophes and symbols part words; the whole word "saint" read as "st", so "Saint Martin" and "St. Martin" are both "st martin" while "Saints" and "Sainte" stay; and one space between words, none at the ends. Beside it, `matchesSearch(text, query)`, both normalised, holds when every word of the search starts a word of the text, in any order, so "morph" finds "paul morphy open" and "orphy" does not, and a word that is only the start of "saint", such as "sain", finds neither "Saint" nor "St." until it is whole, while the word "st", which "Saint" and "St." both read as, finds only the whole word "st", so a search for Saint finds St. Tammany and never State, Street or Stanley; and `SEARCH_QUERY_MIN` and `SEARCH_QUERY_MAX`, 2 and 64, counted in characters of the normalised search, not in the code units a letter outside the common range takes two of. The file uses nothing newer than the site's compiler target, ES2020, and is not added to `domain/format/index.ts`; the server imports it by its path, and the site's matching of its own pages will import it as `@domain/format/searchText` from WS02 step 11. `test/unit/domain-shims.test.ts` gives each of the two one home, so no second definition can appear in the site, the server, the workers or the scripts, and `test/unit/format-edges.test.ts` lists the file among `domain/format`'s. No read uses LIKE: SQLite's `lower()` and `LIKE` fold the plain letters alone and see no stripped mark, no "&" for "and" and no "Saint" for "St", so a filter on a stored name with the search's words would drop rows the normaliser matches, a stored "Jean-Étienne Open" for "etienne" and a stored "Saint Martin Open" for "st martin"; each read is bounded instead, by its window, its columns and 500 rows. In the search's integration tests the six reads returned, from that file's database of the migrations' rows and its own: 19 upcoming events, 11 results, 4 partner events, 39 clubs, 12 posts and 159 pairs of a year and a title from the honor roll.
- **The endpoint.** `functions/api/search.ts` holds the page alone, `onRequestOptions` and `onRequestGet`, which hands the request and the edge's cache to `answerSearch`; the reads, the answer and the cache are in `functions/utils/search.ts`, beside it, so the unit tests reach each part. The search is `q`, the first if the address names two, normalised; one of fewer than 2 or more than 64 characters once normalised (a lone letter, 65 letters, punctuation alone, an empty `q` or none) answers 400 with `{ error: 'Search for 2 to 64 letters or numbers.' }`, the body every error has, kept nowhere. The answer is brief 1.4's SearchResponse: `q`, the search as normalised, the one text every search that normalises alike shares, and the groups that hold a match, in the brief's order, Tournaments, Clubs, News, Results and Champions, each with its heading's words, at most 5 a group and 20 in all, each group's first five in its own order and a later group taking what the earlier ones leave, so with five full groups the Champions group gets none; a group with no match is left out, never sent empty. Each row has an `id` unique in the answer (`event:` and the tournament's id in either group, `partner:`, `club:`, `news:` and the post's slug, and `champions:` with the list, the year and the title as normalised, never a row's own id), a `title`, a `meta` line of parts joined by a middle dot, an `href`, and where it applies a `tag` or `external: true`. An LCA event: "Fixture Fall Open", "Sat, Nov 14, 2026 · Kenner, LA", its page, tagged "Registration open", and one of two days "Sat, Nov 14, 2026 to Sun, Nov 15, 2026 · Kenner, LA". A partner event: "Fixture Coast Open", "Fri, Nov 20, 2026 · Biloxi, MS", its organizer's page and `external: true`. A club: its name, "Monroe · North Louisiana" and its page. A post: its title, "Tue, Oct 20, 2026" and its page. A result: its name, its last day and its place, the event's page, tagged "Final standings". A champions row: "2026 Louisiana State Champion", "State champions" and `/champions#state-champions`. An upcoming LCA event's tag reads its registration as the registration endpoint itself decides it: "Registration open" while it is open and its close time, read on Louisiana's clock, has not passed, "Registration closed" when it is closed or that time has passed, and "Opens soon" for a draft, the words of the site's status badge, which `test/unit/search.test.ts` holds the server's to; a result's is "Final standings", the tone WS02 step 10 draws. No row holds a count, a fee, a capacity, a description, an organizer, a contact or an email. Each group's order: the LCA events by their first day and then their name, then the partner rows; the clubs by name, as the clubs page lists them; the posts newest first; the results the latest last day first; and the champions by year, newest first, the state list before the scholastic one. A row is matched on its own words alone: an event by its name and place, a result by those and the year of its last day, a partner event by its name, city and state, a club by its name, city and region, a post by its title, and a champions row by its year and title. The six reads, `tournaments` twice (its upcoming rows and its results, each with its own window, its own order and its own bound) and the clearinghouse, the clubs, the posts and the honor roll once each, name their columns, bind every value, take at most 500 rows each and go to the database in one `db.batch`, a single round trip.
- **The windows and the Central day.** Today is Louisiana's calendar day, `centralToday`, from `zonedParts` and `LCA_TIME_ZONE` (`domain/format/date.ts` and `centralTime.ts`, imported and not edited, since the daily-emails worker bundles them), worked out once a request from the clock and bound to the reads as a value, never SQLite's `date('now')`, which is UTC's day; `functions/api/clearinghouse.ts` uses that at its line 60, its partner rows' first day against UTC's date, and is left as it is. From today, `searchWindows` gives the earliest last day of a result, the same day three years before, and the earliest day a post shown was published, the same day 24 months before, both counted in, a leap day going to the last day of a February that has none (Tuesday, February 29, 2028 gives Friday, February 28, 2025 and Saturday, February 28, 2026). An event's last day is its end date, or its first day when it has none or an empty one. A listed LCA event is in Tournaments when its last day is today or later, in Results when its last day is before today and on or after the day three years before, and in neither when it is older or not a day as the database writes days; one day decides both, so no event is in two groups. The status is not read for it: an event marked completed before its day is still upcoming, and one left as upcoming after its day is a result, by its dates; the schema has no cancelled status, the tournaments' check allowing upcoming, active and completed alone, so none is left out for one. A partner event is upcoming until its last day has passed, so one under way stays. A post shows when it is published and its day is on or after the day 24 months before, with no upper bound, as the news list shows a published post whatever its date.
